title: Ball Stuck in a Tree - What Are Your Options?
question: Your tee shot becomes lodged high up in a tree and you cannot play it where it lies. What are your options?

choices.text: Take free relief because the ball is impossible to play.
Shake the tree until the ball falls out.
Declare the ball lost and play another ball.
Either try to play the ball as it lies (for example by shaking the tree or climbing it if safe), or take unplayable ball relief with a one-stroke penalty.

explanation: A ball stuck in a tree is not lost if its location is known or virtually certain. The player may play the ball as it lies, which could include shaking the tree in an attempt to dislodge the ball, provided no rule is infringed (such as deliberately breaking branches to improve conditions). Alternatively, unplayable ball relief may be taken anywhere on the course except in a penalty area, with a one-stroke penalty. There is no free relief simply for a ball stuck in a tree.
